title: Pasta e Fagioli Veneta
subtitle: Venetian pasta and borlotti bean soup
excerpt: Pasta e fagioli is a thick, hearty soup of borlotti beans and small pasta. The Venetian version uses fresh or dried borlotti beans, a soffritto of onion, celery, carrot and pancetta, and small pasta stirred in at the end. Half the beans are pureed to thicken the soup. It sits between a soup and a pasta dish.
sourceNotes: Pasta e fagioli is one of the great cucina povera dishes of Italy, made across the whole country from Venice to Naples. The Venetian version is characterised by the use of borlotti beans, pancetta, and rosemary. It is a winter dish, traditionally thick enough that a spoon stands up in it.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the pasta. Reheat and add freshly cooked pasta when serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch of the bean soup and freeze without pasta.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Improves overnight. Add the pasta only when reheating to serve.

content.text: The technique of pureeing half the beans is what gives pasta e fagioli its distinctive thick, creamy consistency while still having whole beans for texture. The pasta is added at the end and cooked in the soup, so it absorbs some of the liquid and thickens the dish further. Use a short pasta: pasta-dried, tubetti, or small rigatoni.

items.prepNote: or other small pasta such as tubetti
rind saved for cooking, grated to serve

content.text: Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} olive oil in a large heavy pan over medium heat. Add {{pancetta}} pancetta and cook for 3 minutes until lightly golden. Add {{onion}} onion, {{celery}} celery, and {{carrot}} carrot. Cook for 10 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} garlic and {{rosemary}} rosemary sprigs and cook for 1 minute.

Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Add {{borlotti-beans}} borlotti beans and 1.5 litres of water. Add the Parmesan rind if using. Season with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Simmer for 25 minutes.
Remove the rosemary and Parmesan rind. Remove half the beans with a ladle, mash them roughly or blend briefly, and return to the pot. This thickens the soup without making it completely smooth.

Add {{pasta-dried}} pasta and cook in the soup for 8 to 10 minutes until just tender. The soup will be very thick. Add a splash of water if it becomes too thick. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil and {{parmesan}} Parmesan.

items.symptom: The pasta absorbed all the liquid overnight
items.cause: Pasta continues to absorb liquid as the soup sits.
items.fix: Add pasta only when ready to serve. If reheating a dish that has thickened overnight, add water or stock and bring back to a simmer, then taste for seasoning before serving.

content.text: Pasta e fagioli is one of the defining dishes of Italian cucina povera -- cheap, filling, and made from beans and pasta that keep all winter. The Venetian version uses borlotti beans, which are grown in the Veneto and Friuli. The dish is thick enough in the Venetian tradition that it is eaten with a fork, not a spoon, and served on a plate, not in a bowl. Every family has a version; every version is slightly different.
